answer.rationale: b1 documents that a prior rollback cleared a write-path error spike cleanly with no customer impact; b6 confirms staged gating has caught regressions before, so a guarded partial rollback is precedented and low-risk. Pinning the security patch via selective revert (or a forward fix for only the offending component) keeps compliance satisfied since the patch is preserved. This is the single intervention most likely to restore p99 quickly without losing in-flight settlement writes; add_capacity, failover, circuit breaker, and read-replica routing are all slower-acting or don't address a release-driven regression in a peak write window. b1 is verified first to confirm the rollback procedure and its blast radius before committing.
